blocks.text: 1. Knowledge Graphs
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862667-370826754.png

Function Calling closed the Agentic RAG module with a strict, schema-validated interface for invoking a function. Knowledge Graphs, structured networks of entities and the relationships connecting them, open this dedicated Graph RAG module by defining the data structure everything else in it depends on.
A knowledge graph represents facts as nodes and edges rather than as free-form text passages.
2. Nodes Represent Entities
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862668-926919914.png
As covered generally in Graph RAG, a knowledge graph node represents one distinct real-world thing, such as a person, product, or company.
Each node typically carries a type and a set of properties describing that thing.
3. Edges Represent Relationships
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862668-820130275.png
A knowledge graph edge connects two nodes and names the specific relationship between them.
It is a labeled, directed connection, not just an unlabeled line between two things.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Graph element","What it represents"],"rows":[["Node","One distinct real-world entity"],["Edge","A named, directed relationship between two nodes"]]}

blocks.text: 4. Facts As Connected Triples
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862669-485183984.png
A single fact can be written as a subject, a relationship, and an object, forming one triple.
A whole knowledge graph is simply a large collection of these triples linked together.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: The fact that Falcon Cloud supplies Acme Corp is one triple: Falcon Cloud as the subject, supplies as the relationship, and Acme Corp as the object, the smallest unit a knowledge graph is built from.

blocks.text: 5. Why Free Text Loses Structure
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862860-237526961.png
As with chunks versus connected entities in Graph RAG, a fact buried inside a paragraph of free text is hard to query precisely.
The same fact expressed as a triple can be queried directly and exactly.
6. A Schema Constrains What Can Be Expressed

blocks.alt: A Schema Constrains What Can Be Expressed
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862862-575822213.png
As with a structured schema defining valid relationships in Knowledge Graph RAG, a schema defines the allowed node types and relationship types upfront.
This keeps the graph consistent rather than letting it accumulate arbitrary, inconsistent connections.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Consistency"],"rows":[["No schema","Arbitrary, potentially inconsistent connections"],["Defined schema","Consistent node and relationship types enforced upfront"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Knowledge Graphs Versus Relational Tables
A relational table represents relationships implicitly through shared key columns.
A knowledge graph instead represents each relationship as its own explicit, named edge.
8. Populating A Graph Takes Real Work
As with knowledge graph construction being the main cost in Knowledge Graph RAG, building a graph of real triples from raw source material is nontrivial engineering.
Entity extraction and relation extraction, covered next in this module, are the specific steps that do this work.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A knowledge graph does not build itself from raw documents automatically; entity extraction and relation extraction, the next two topics in this module, are the specific processes that turn raw text into real triples.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When A Knowledge Graph Is The Right Structure For The Data

blocks.alt: Recognizing When A Knowledge Graph Is The Right Structure For The Data
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862862-978790323.png
Domains rich in named entities and explicit relationships suit a knowledge graph well.
Unstructured, loosely connected prose, by contrast, is often better served by plain chunk retrieval.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Treating a knowledge graph as unlabeled connections instead of named, directed relationships.
Skipping a schema and letting arbitrary, inconsistent node and relationship types accumulate.
Assuming a knowledge graph builds itself automatically from raw source documents.
Choosing a knowledge graph for unstructured prose that plain chunk retrieval would serve better.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: A knowledge graph represents facts as nodes and edges rather than free-form text passages.
A node represents one distinct real-world entity, typically with a type and properties.
An edge is a labeled, directed connection naming the specific relationship between two nodes.
A fact can be written as a subject, relationship, and object triple, the graph's smallest unit.
A fact buried in free text is hard to query precisely; the same fact as a triple is queried exactly.
A schema defines allowed node and relationship types upfront, keeping the graph consistent.
A knowledge graph represents relationships explicitly as edges, unlike implicit relational table keys.
Building a real graph of triples from raw source material is nontrivial engineering work.
